subject: Questions mediation analysis and fit indices (from someone who is new to Lavaan)

messages.author: 103216590b55b6a4
messages.subject: Questions mediation analysis and fit indices (from someone who is new to Lavaan)
parts:
Hi all,
I’m new to R/Lavaan and I have a few questions about mediation models that I wanted to test (for instance, to examine whether maladaptive schemas mediate the association between attachment anxiety and internalizing problems). I used FIML to impute the missing data and requested bootstrap standard errors. I have included the syntax of one of the models that I want to test below.

Just to be sure, I was wondering whether the syntax to test this models looks correct according to you?

Besides, I have a question about the fit indices. When I had a look at the fit indices, I got some ‘strange’ results (“perfect” fit indices) e.g., CFI = 1, RMSEA = 0 and Chi squared = 0. And I’m not sure whether this suggest that I did something incorrectly, or whether these values of the fit indices are plausible?

My final question concerns the 95% CI of the parameter estimate of the indirect effect. I inspect these CIs my models to evaluate the significance of the indirect effects. However, I am not sure which type of CIs LAVAAN generates by default (bias-corrected CI, or another type?)?

Thanks in advance for your help!! Chloë

 

Syntax of one of the models that I fitted:

 

Model1 <- '

W5Internalizing~ c*W1Anxiety + b*W4Schemas

W4Schemas ~ a* W1Anxiety

# indirect effect (a*b)

ab := a*b

# total effect

Total := c + (a*b)

'

fit1A <- sem(Model1 , data = EMSdata, missing = "ML", se = "bootstrap")

 

summary(Model1, fit.measures = TRUE)

parameterestimates(Model1)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Questions mediation analysis and fit indices (from someone who is new to Lavaan)
parts: I used FIML to impute the missing data
FIML is not imputation.  It merely uses all available information per case to estimate parameters.
I was wondering whether the syntax to test this models looks correct according to you?
You mean the indirect and total effects?  Yes, the parameter labels are consistent with a textbook 3-variable mediation model.

When I had a look at the fit indices, I got some ‘strange’ results (“perfect” fit indices) e.g., CFI = 1, RMSEA = 0 and Chi squared = 0. And I’m not sure whether this suggest that I did something incorrectly, or whether these values of the fit indices are plausible?

You only have 3 variables, and you estimate the relationship between each pair, so your model is saturated (df = 0).  Fit will be arbitrarily perfect.  All you can do is interpret and test individual parameters.

My final question concerns the 95% CI of the parameter estimate of the indirect effect. I inspect these CIs my models to evaluate the significance of the indirect effects. However, I am not sure which type of CIs LAVAAN generates by default (bias-corrected CI, or another type?)?

By default, they are percentile intervals, but you can change that.  Read the ?parameterEstimates help page.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
